transcript:
Meeting: Discovery - Buying Redwood via AWS Marketplace (HelioBank)
Date: Jan 16, 2025
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 41 min
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

Attendees:
- Jordan Blake (Redwood Inference, GTM)
- Markus Klein (Redwood Inference, Solutions Engineering)
- Naomi Feldman (Redwood Inference, Product - Security/Compliance)
- Elena Rossi (HelioBank, Platform Engineering)
- Samir Khan (HelioBank, Security Engineering)
- Priya Desai (HelioBank, Procurement)
- Tom Weller (HelioBank, Data Engineering)

---
Auto Summary (generated)
HelioBank is evaluating Redwood Inference for LLM inference and prefers purchasing through AWS Marketplace for committed spend and invoicing. HelioBank asked for clarity on Redwood’s Marketplace SKUs (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security posture (SOC 2, encryption/KMS, audit logging, retention controls, data residency), and the purchase-to-provisioning flow (entitlements mapping to a Redwood org, region alignment, activation time). Redwood outlined the marketplace packaging approach, shared responsibility boundaries, and proposed next steps: share SKU guidance, send security FAQ / evidence request process, and schedule a technical deep dive.

Topics
- Procurement path via AWS Marketplace (private offer, committed spend)
- SKU mapping: Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private (VPC)
- Security requirements: SOC 2, encryption, KMS/HSM, audit logs, retention/residency
- Onboarding flow: entitlement activation, org linking, region constraints
- Pilot criteria: latency, throughput, and success metrics

Questions captured
- Does Redwood support VPC deployment purchased via AWS Marketplace, or is it hosted-only?
- How are audit logs exposed and what is retained by default?
- Can HelioBank restrict inference to specific AWS regions?
- How long after purchase until entitlements are active and the org is linked?

---
Transcript

[00:00] Jordan Blake: Alright, looks like we’re at time. Thanks everyone for joining. I’m Jordan, I run a lot of our enterprise procurement and marketplace motions. Markus is on solutions engineering, and Naomi is here because I saw security requirements in the notes.

[00:14] Elena Rossi: Yep, hi. I’m Elena, platform engineering. We’re the team that would own the integration and—like—runtime choices.

[00:21] Samir Khan: Samir, security engineering.

[00:23] Priya Desai: Hi, Priya, procurement.

[00:25] Tom Weller: Tom, data engineering. I’m more on the pipelines side.

[00:29] Jordan Blake: Great. Maybe to kick off, Elena, can you give us the “why now” and what you’re trying to buy through marketplace?

[00:38] Elena Rossi: Sure. We have a couple internal copilots we’re rolling out. We started with, like, Azure OpenAI, but for a bunch of reasons we’re standardizing on AWS for the rest of the year. And procurement basically said if it’s not on AWS Marketplace it’s… painful.

[00:53] Priya Desai: Not impossible, but yes, slower.

[00:56] Jordan Blake: Totally. That’s a very common constraint. When you say “buy through AWS Marketplace,” is the driver committed spend, consolidated billing, PO-to-invoice, or all of the above?

[01:08] Priya Desai: All of the above. We have a spend commitment we need to burn down. Also it’s just the vendor onboarding and payment terms. Marketplace is pre-approved.

[01:18] Jordan Blake: Got it. That’s helpful. And then on the technical side—Markus can ask some of the workload questions—but at a high level are you thinking: hosted API (you call us over the internet), or do you need VPC / private deployment?

[01:33] Elena Rossi: We likely need VPC. For some workloads we can do hosted, but anything with customer data is going to trigger a whole… process.

[01:42] Samir Khan: If it’s public endpoints, we need compensating controls, and it’s a long review.

[01:46] Jordan Blake: Understood. Naomi, do you want to set context on what we can and can’t claim here, and then we can go deeper?

[01:53] Naomi Feldman: Yeah. So we have three broad modes: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployment. Private is the one where we can do customer-managed networking in a VPC—typically that’s what folks mean by “VPC deployment.” The details depend on the region and connectivity pattern (PrivateLink vs peering vs customer-managed egress), but directionally yes.

[02:16] Elena Rossi: And can that be purchased via AWS Marketplace? Or does it have to be direct contract?

[02:22] Jordan Blake: It can be purchased via AWS Marketplace. Sometimes we do it as a private offer, depending on the commercial structure. But yes, we can align it so it draws down your AWS commit.

[02:32] Priya Desai: Okay. Private offer is fine. We usually do that anyway.

[02:36] Markus Klein: On the technical side, I just want to confirm: when you say VPC, is your goal that inference endpoints are only reachable from your VPC, no public internet, and ideally logs also stay within your boundaries?

[02:48] Elena Rossi: Yes, and region constrained. We’re mostly us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

[02:54] Samir Khan: And encryption. KMS keys, audit logs, the usual.

[02:58] Markus Klein: Yep.

[03:00] Jordan Blake: Maybe we should clarify SKUs because marketplace tends to make this confusing. Today we think of it as: Hosted API SKU, Dedicated SKU, and Private SKU, and then add-ons like compliance retention or premium SLA. That’s the structure we’re aligning to.

[03:17] Priya Desai: For procurement, we’ll need something that maps cleanly to your invoice line items. Like, what are we actually buying? Tokens, capacity, or license?

[03:26] Jordan Blake: Great question. Hosted is typically usage-based. Dedicated is reserved capacity. Private tends to be a platform fee plus support tier, and then usage or capacity depending on the setup. Marketplace can represent these as contracted dimensions. We’ll give you a SKU mapping doc.

[03:44] Tom Weller: When you say “usage-based,” are you metering per token?

[03:47] Markus Klein: For Hosted, yes, per-token and other meters depending on endpoint type (embeddings vs generation). For Dedicated/Private, we often anchor on capacity because you want predictable throughput.

[04:00] Elena Rossi: The reason we’re talking is we saw Redwood had better performance on open models than… some of the others. We tried Together for a bit. And Bedrock is… fine but we don’t get enough knobs.

[04:13] Markus Klein: Makes sense. When you say performance, what’s your top metric? Latency p95? Cost per token? Throughput? Or “all of it.”

[04:21] Elena Rossi: p95 latency for interactive, but we also have batch summarization. So two profiles.

[04:28] Markus Klein: Cool. Roughly what context lengths? Like 4k, 16k, 32k?

[04:33] Tom Weller: For the copilot, 8k-ish now, but we’ll push 16k.

[04:38] Markus Klein: Great.

[04:40] Jordan Blake: Priya, on marketplace—do you need it to be a public listing purchase, or can it be a private offer that references the listing?

[04:48] Priya Desai: Private offer that references the listing is fine. We generally want the “paper trail” in marketplace so finance is happy.

[04:56] Jordan Blake: Perfect.

[05:00] Samir Khan: I want to be direct: we will ask for SOC 2 Type II, plus a pen test letter, and we’ll ask about encryption at rest and in transit. And audit logging—like who did what.

[05:12] Naomi Feldman: Totally fair. We can share SOC 2 under NDA. We do encryption in transit (TLS) and encryption at rest. For key management, we integrate with cloud KMS. The exact key custody model depends on Hosted vs Private. We should be careful: for Hosted, keys are managed by Redwood in our accounts with KMS controls; for Private, we can support customer-managed keys in your account in some configurations.

[05:40] Samir Khan: So hosted is not customer-managed keys.

[05:43] Naomi Feldman: Correct, generally not “your KMS key,” unless it’s a dedicated/private pattern. I can follow up with the exact supported configurations.

[05:52] Elena Rossi: For audit logs, do we get like CloudTrail? Or is it your audit logs?

[05:57] Naomi Feldman: It’s Redwood audit logs for application-level events—org admin changes, API key creation, SSO changes, model deployment changes, things like that. For infrastructure-level logs, in Private we can integrate more deeply. We do not present it as “your CloudTrail,” it’s more: we provide audit log exports and retention options.

[06:20] Markus Klein: And from an ops perspective, the Console shows per-route usage, latency, errors, and you can stream logs to your SIEM depending on plan.

[06:30] Samir Khan: Retention period?

[06:33] Naomi Feldman: Default retention depends on SKU. There’s an add-on for extended retention. I want to be precise: we have baseline operational logs retention and then a separate longer retention option for audit log history. I’ll send the FAQ with the numbers we’re allowed to commit to publicly.

[06:53] Jordan Blake: That’s a good segue. Marketplace listings sometimes require a security FAQ attachment. We have one tailored for marketplace buyers, and we’ll provide it.

[07:03] Priya Desai: Also, data residency. We have EU requirements.

[07:07] Naomi Feldman: Yep. We can pin inference to specific regions. The statement we typically use is: data is processed in the selected region and we have controls to prevent cross-region processing, but some metadata (like billing) may be global depending on system. I’ll send the exact wording that’s been reviewed.

[07:30] Elena Rossi: What about the data itself—prompts and completions. Do you store them?

[07:36] Markus Klein: By default, we don’t use customer prompts/completions to train models. For storage, we have configurable logging. In Hosted, you can disable payload logging, and we keep minimal operational metadata. For Private, it’s more customizable, but again Naomi can give the authoritative version.

[07:56] Samir Khan: We’ll need that in writing.

[07:58] Naomi Feldman: Absolutely.

[08:00] Jordan Blake: Let’s talk about the purchase-to-provisioning flow because that’s where buyers get stuck. Are you expecting a self-serve “click buy and it just works,” or do you anticipate a coordinated onboarding?

[08:12] Elena Rossi: Ideally click buy. Realistically we’ll coordinate because of the VPC pieces.

[08:18] Jordan Blake: Great. The flow is basically: you purchase in AWS Marketplace, AWS sends an entitlement event, we map that to a Redwood org. You either create a new Redwood org during linking or link to an existing one. Then you select region(s) and deployment mode. For Private there’s a setup step.

[08:37] Tom Weller: How long does entitlement activation take? Some marketplaces take hours.

[08:42] Jordan Blake: Usually minutes. There are edge cases where it can lag; we have monitoring and a support escalation. For enterprise buyers we also proactively watch the first purchase.

[08:53] Priya Desai: Do you need our AWS account ID to link?

[08:56] Jordan Blake: Yes, typically the purchaser account. And we’ll also ask for a Redwood admin email for the org owner. We try not to collect more than needed.

[09:07] Markus Klein: For region, Elena, you mentioned us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Are you expecting to run both, or start with one?

[09:14] Elena Rossi: Start with us-east-1, then EU shortly after.

[09:19] Markus Klein: Okay. We can plan a pilot with one region pinned, then expand.

[09:24] Samir Khan: For Private, is it like you deploy into our account? Or you run in your account but reachable via private networking?

[09:33] Markus Klein: Good question. There are a couple patterns. Most commonly, the control plane is managed by Redwood and the data plane is isolated with dedicated capacity and private networking. Some customers want a full “in your account” model; that gets closer to on-prem style and is more complex. We can talk through what’s needed.

[09:55] Elena Rossi: We probably want “in our VPC but you manage it.” Like we don’t want to run GPUs.

[10:01] Markus Klein: That’s the common ask.

[10:04] Jordan Blake: And from a marketplace SKU standpoint, that maps cleanly to our Private offering.

[10:10] Priya Desai: How do upgrades work? Like if we start hosted and then move to private, is that a new purchase?

[10:17] Jordan Blake: We can structure it as an upgrade. Operationally it’s a plan transition; on marketplace it can be a new dimension or a new private offer. We’ll propose the cleanest path with finance.

[10:32] Priya Desai: Okay, because we have internal rules about canceling and re-buying.

[10:36] Jordan Blake: Yep, understood.

[10:40] Markus Klein: Elena, can I ask: what’s the current model set? Are you looking at Llama variants, Mistral, something else?

[10:47] Tom Weller: Mostly Llama 70B class, and some smaller for routing. We also looked at rerankers.

[10:54] Markus Klein: Great, we support that. And we have structured output, tool calling, streaming, all the standard API stuff.

[11:03] Elena Rossi: If we buy via marketplace, do we lose features? Some vendors do that.

[11:08] Jordan Blake: No, the marketplace purchase is just the billing/procurement rail. You get the same product surface. The only nuance is: how entitlements are represented and possibly support tier selection.

[11:21] Samir Khan: Support contacts—do we get a security contact? Like security@ vendor.

[11:26] Naomi Feldman: Yes, we have a security contact channel and an incident response process. Also if you have a vendor questionnaire we can route it.

[11:36] Priya Desai: We’ll have one.

[11:38] Jordan Blake: Great.

[11:40] Markus Klein: Can we talk success criteria for the pilot? Like what would make you say yes.

[11:46] Elena Rossi: We need two things: (1) latency. We’re seeing p95 around 2.5 seconds on some endpoints. We want under 1.5 for typical prompts. (2) The procurement path needs to be marketplace.

[12:02] Markus Klein: And concurrency / throughput? Any rough numbers.

[12:06] Tom Weller: At launch, maybe 50 concurrent for interactive. Batch is like… we can queue it.

[12:13] Markus Klein: Okay that’s manageable.

[12:15] Naomi Feldman: From security side, what are the “must haves” to get through review? If we know the gating items we can preempt.

[12:24] Samir Khan: SOC 2. Encryption at rest/in transit. Audit logs. SSO/SAML eventually. And data retention controls. Plus we’ll ask if you use our data to train.

[12:39] Naomi Feldman: Great. SOC 2 we have. Encryption yes. Audit logs yes. SSO/SAML is supported; details depend on plan. Training: no training on your data by default. Retention controls: we have baseline and add-ons.

[12:56] Samir Khan: Any sub-processors? Like third-party analytics.

[13:01] Naomi Feldman: Yes, we have a list. For marketplace we typically include a subprocessor list link. I’ll share it.

[13:09] Elena Rossi: Can we bring our own model? Like custom weights.

[13:13] Markus Klein: Potentially, in Private. In Hosted we keep a curated catalog. In Private we can onboard models, subject to review and performance validation.

[13:25] Elena Rossi: Okay.

[13:27] Jordan Blake: One other marketplace-specific question: do you need “seller of record” to be AWS, or can Redwood be the vendor? In marketplace, it’s typically AWS billing but Redwood as seller.

[13:38] Priya Desai: As long as it’s on the AWS invoice and counts toward our commit, we’re good.

[13:44] Jordan Blake: Perfect.

[13:46] Markus Klein: Samir, any constraints on public endpoints? If Hosted is used for non-sensitive, is that allowed?

[13:53] Samir Khan: Possibly, but we need IP allowlisting or some control. Otherwise it’s a “no.”

[14:00] Markus Klein: Understood. We can support network restrictions in Dedicated/Private more strongly. For Hosted, we rely on auth (keys, org policies) and can discuss additional controls.

[14:14] Elena Rossi: We’d rather avoid mixed modes initially. Just pick one and go.

[14:18] Markus Klein: Makes sense.

[14:20] Jordan Blake: So it sounds like: Private deployment, purchased via AWS Marketplace, likely via private offer, initial region us-east-1, then EU.

[14:30] Elena Rossi: Yes.

[14:31] Priya Desai: Yes.

[14:33] Jordan Blake: Great. Markus, anything else you need to scope for a follow-on technical session?

[14:38] Markus Klein: Yeah, just a few quick ones. (1) peak tokens per second target, (2) max context length, (3) model list, (4) whether you need embeddings and reranking in the same environment.

[14:51] Tom Weller: We need embeddings too. Reranking maybe later.

[14:56] Markus Klein: Great. We can cover that.

[14:59] Samir Khan: I also want to understand incident response. Like breach notification windows.

[15:05] Naomi Feldman: That’s typically in our security packet and contractual terms. For marketplace, we align with standard enterprise terms but exact notification windows are contract-specific. We can share our standard language for review.

[15:20] Priya Desai: Okay.

[15:22] Jordan Blake: On the commercial side, do you already know a budget range? Even a ballpark helps so we don’t propose something that doesn’t fit.

[15:31] Priya Desai: Not yet. We have capacity, but we need a proposal to start. Maybe in the low seven figures annual, depending.

[15:40] Jordan Blake: That’s helpful. We can work with that.

[15:44] Elena Rossi: We also need a timeline. We want something running in six weeks.

[15:49] Jordan Blake: Six weeks is doable if we treat it like a pilot and parallelize security review with technical setup.

[15:56] Markus Klein: Agreed.

[16:00] (crosstalk)

[16:01] Jordan Blake: Sorry—go ahead.

[16:03] Samir Khan: Our security review alone can take three to four weeks.

[16:06] Jordan Blake: Yep. That’s why we’ll send the packet early.

[16:10] Naomi Feldman: If you can tell us the questionnaire format, we can pre-fill what we already have.

[16:15] Priya Desai: We have a standard SIG-lite and a data processing addendum.

[16:20] Naomi Feldman: Great.

[16:22] Markus Klein: While Samir is here, one detail: do you require SAML on day one?

[16:28] Samir Khan: For production, yes. For pilot, maybe not, but it helps.

[16:32] Naomi Feldman: Understood. We can enable SAML. We’ll confirm which SKUs include it.

[16:40] Elena Rossi: Another question: do you have any “model fallback” behavior? Like if a region is out, does it fail over?

[16:47] Markus Klein: Yes, we have routing policies and fallbacks, but in Private it’s configured. Some customers prefer strict region pinning with no cross-region. We can do both; it’s a policy choice.

[17:02] Samir Khan: No cross-region for us.

[17:04] Markus Klein: Great, that’s straightforward.

[17:07] Jordan Blake: Cool. Priya, for marketplace, we’ll likely propose: base Private SKU plus add-ons like extended audit retention if needed, and potentially premium SLA. Does your procurement team care if those are separate line items?

[17:20] Priya Desai: Separate is okay, but fewer is better.

[17:24] Jordan Blake: Got it.

[17:26] Markus Klein: Elena, do you have a sense of environment separation? Like dev/stage/prod.

[17:31] Elena Rossi: We’ll want at least non-prod and prod. Maybe three.

[17:36] Markus Klein: Okay. That impacts sizing and cost.

[17:40] Jordan Blake: We can structure that as one contract with multiple environments, or separate—depends on your preference.

[17:47] Tom Weller: For batch, can we do asynchronous jobs or is it all request/response?

[17:52] Markus Klein: We support streaming request/response. For async, folks usually integrate with their own queue and call us; we can share best practices.

[18:03] Tom Weller: Okay.

[18:05] Naomi Feldman: One more compliance question: do you have requirements like PCI or HIPAA?

[18:10] Samir Khan: Not HIPAA. PCI is relevant, yes.

[18:14] Naomi Feldman: Understood. We’re not going to claim PCI certification for the product unless it’s explicitly covered; we can discuss controls alignment.

[18:23] Samir Khan: Fine.

[18:25] Jordan Blake: Let me check time. We have about 20 minutes. I think the remaining key thing is: what do we need to do for the marketplace path so this doesn’t stall.

[18:34] Priya Desai: We need: vendor name, listing link, product description, support contacts, pricing structure, and security docs.

[18:44] Jordan Blake: Great. We’ll send a package: listing overview + SKU guidance + security FAQ and instructions for requesting SOC 2. Then we can start a private offer conversation.

[18:58] Elena Rossi: Can we see a demo? Like the Console and the org linking flow?

[19:03] Markus Klein: Yes. We can do a demo in the technical deep dive. We’ll show how marketplace entitlements appear, and how you link your AWS purchase to your Redwood org.

[19:15] Elena Rossi: That would help. Our fear is we buy and then it’s like “open a ticket.”

[19:20] Jordan Blake: Totally. We’re specifically improving that flow. The goal is minimal tickets.

[19:26] Samir Khan: Are there audit logs for that linking action?

[19:30] Naomi Feldman: Yes, org linking and entitlement changes are audited.

[19:34] Samir Khan: Great.

[19:36] Markus Klein: Also, region mismatch is a common issue—like you buy in one region but try to deploy in another. We’ll show guardrails and error messages.

[19:47] Elena Rossi: Good.

[19:49] Priya Desai: On pricing, can you give a rough estimate or do we need to go through a whole scoping.

[19:55] Jordan Blake: For Private we’ll need a little scoping, but we can give a range quickly once we have model + throughput + environments.

[20:05] Tom Weller: What’s the minimal info you need?

[20:07] Markus Klein: (1) Model(s), (2) max context length, (3) concurrency, (4) target p95, (5) which region(s), (6) non-prod/prod split.

[20:18] Tom Weller: Okay.

[20:20] Samir Khan: And security: do you have a standard DPA?

[20:24] Jordan Blake: Yes, we do.

[20:26] Priya Desai: We’ll need to route that through legal but if it’s marketplace sometimes it’s standardized.

[20:32] Jordan Blake: Exactly. Some items are standardized in marketplace terms, but we can still attach addenda depending on the structure.

[20:42] Elena Rossi: Is there anything in the marketplace that blocks a VPC deployment? Like does AWS treat it differently?

[20:49] Jordan Blake: No, marketplace is just the procurement rail. The deployment details are separate.

[20:55] Markus Klein: Right, and sometimes the marketplace listing is “software as a service” category. That’s okay.

[21:02] Samir Khan: SaaS category is okay if we can show controls.

[21:06] Naomi Feldman: Yep.

[21:08] Jordan Blake: Let’s do a quick recap and then open questions. My recap: HelioBank wants Private (VPC), wants marketplace purchase and likely private offer, needs security packet (SOC 2 etc.), wants region pinning to us-east-1 and then eu-west-1, and success criteria is p95 latency improvements plus procurement path.

[21:28] Elena Rossi: Accurate.

[21:30] Priya Desai: Yep.

[21:32] Jordan Blake: Cool. Questions we didn’t cover?

[21:35] Tom Weller: Do you support embeddings and generation in the same deployment? Or separate clusters.

[21:41] Markus Klein: We can do both. Sometimes we separate for efficiency, but it’s not required.

[21:47] Elena Rossi: How quickly can we start a pilot after paperwork.

[21:51] Jordan Blake: If we get a private offer accepted within a week or two, we can start provisioning quickly. We’ll parallelize technical validation.

[21:59] Samir Khan: We’ll need to review the security docs before pilot hits real data.

[22:03] Jordan Blake: Totally.

[22:05] Naomi Feldman: I’ll send the marketplace security FAQ today or tomorrow. For SOC 2, we’ll need NDA. I’ll include the request process.

[22:14] Priya Desai: Okay.

[22:16] Markus Klein: And I’ll send a short sizing questionnaire.

[22:20] Jordan Blake: Perfect. Priya, is there anyone else we should loop in? Finance? Cloud center of excellence?

[22:27] Priya Desai: Finance will get involved once we see the offer. CCoE maybe, but Elena can pull them in.

[22:34] Elena Rossi: Yeah, we can.

[22:36] Jordan Blake: Great.

[22:38] (brief silence)

[22:40] Elena Rossi: One last: we are evaluating Anyscale too, mostly for “bring your own model.” How do you compare?

[22:48] Markus Klein: We’re focused specifically on inference runtime + operational tooling. If BYOM is important, we can support in Private, but our differentiation is predictable serving—latency, cost controls, and rollouts with observability.

[23:03] Jordan Blake: And on marketplace, we try to make procurement clean. That’s a big theme.

[23:09] Elena Rossi: Okay.

[23:10] Samir Khan: Any FedRAMP plans?

[23:13] Naomi Feldman: Not something we can commit to on this call. We can share current compliance posture and roadmap at a high level, but we don’t want to overpromise.

[23:22] Samir Khan: Fine.

[23:24] Jordan Blake: Cool. If no more questions, we’ll send the follow-ups and propose times for the technical deep dive.

[23:31] Elena Rossi: Works.

[23:33] Priya Desai: Thanks.

[23:34] Tom Weller: Thanks.

[23:35] Samir Khan: Thank you.

[23:37] Jordan Blake: Thanks all.

(Recording ended early; remaining time on calendar was unused.)
